claims.text: NbMoCrTiAl is a refractory high-entropy alloy system relevant to high-temperature structural applications.
The lower-aluminum baseline alloy forms a nonuniform or discontinuous oxide scale under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Increasing the aluminum fraction by a few atomic percent will favor alumina formation.
Increasing aluminum content will promote rapid formation of a continuous alumina scale.
The alumina scale produced by increasing aluminum content will adhere to the alloy surface.
A continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface layer acts as a barrier to further oxygen ingress.
Higher aluminum content enhances the kinetics of alumina formation.
An established protective Al2O3 scale reduces oxygen diffusion into the substrate.
Reduced oxygen diffusion prevents further oxidation and stabilizes the alloy surface.
The higher-aluminum alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain than the lower-aluminum alloy.
The higher-aluminum alloy will form a thinner oxide scale than the lower-aluminum alloy.
The higher-aluminum alloy will form a denser and more uniform oxide scale than the lower-aluminum alloy.
The higher-aluminum alloy will exhibit improved microstructural stability during high-temperature oxidation.
The proposed oxidation-resistance improvement is expected at approximately 1100°C in a dry oxidizing atmosphere for about 100 hours.
Interactions with other oxide-forming alloying elements may alter the degree of oxidation-resistance benefit.
The effect of the proposed aluminum increase on mechanical properties has not been fully quantified.
